updates.title: Horse Protection
updates.abstract: On May 8, 2024, the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) of the United States Department of Agriculture published in the Federal Register a final rule that amended the regulations promulgated under the Horse Protection Act (the May 2024 Horse Protection final rule). APHIS is proposing to remove the provisions of the May 2024 Horse Protection final rule that have been vacated by court order and proposing to withdraw the remaining non-vacated provisions of the May 2024 Horse Protection final rule to ensure that the regulations afford due process and better align with the Act. APHIS is also proposing to amend the regulations by revising, among other things, the certification requirements for training and licensing of designated qualified persons (DQPs); enhancing DQP inspection procedures and the process for appealing APHIS inspections before any possible disqualification by management; and clarifying that if a horse is determined to be sore, it is disqualified from participating in the class in which the inspection took place and not the entire event.

updates.title: Mining of Pillars
updates.abstract: MSHA is eliminating outdated requirements for the final mining of pillars from MSHA's regulations. These requirements are being removed because the practice of final mining of pillars with one mine opening is no longer used in the mining industry due to safety concerns.

updates.title: Electrical Equipment for Coal Seams Above the Water Table
updates.abstract: MSHA is removing requirements for the use of permissible electric face equipment in coal seams above the water table. These requirements are being removed from MSHA's regulations because all coal mines are now considered gassy, regardless of location relative to the water table.

updates.title: Improving and Eliminating Regulations; Installation of Foam Generator Systems in Underground Coal Mines
updates.abstract: MSHA is removing outdated requirements regarding the installation of foam generator systems located in underground coal mines. These requirements are being removed from MSHA's regulations because they are no longer applicable.

updates.title: Improving and Eliminating Regulations; Limit on Exposure to Diesel Particulate Matter in Underground Metal and Nonmetal Mines
updates.abstract: MSHA is eliminating outdated requirements for diesel particulate matter (DPM) personal exposure limits for underground metal and nonmetal (MNM) mines. These requirements are being removed from MSHA's regulations because they contain outdated effective dates and exposure limits that are no longer applicable.

updates.title: Improving and Eliminating Regulations; Permissible Lamps in Underground Coal Mines
updates.abstract: MSHA is removing duplicative requirements for electric cap lamps and other electric lamps in underground coal mines. This provision is being removed from MSHA's regulations because it is a duplicative provision and its removal will not reduce the protections afforded to miners.

updates.title: Respirable Crystalline Silica and Respiratory Protection
updates.abstract: This proposed rule clarifies and modifies provisions of the respirable crystalline silica and respiratory protection standards that were established in MSHA's 2024 final rule titled "Lowering Miners' Exposure to Respirable Crystalline Silica and Improving Respiratory Protection." The changes provide clarity and make improvements to the requirements for methods of compliance, exposure monitoring, respiratory protection, medical surveillance, and recordkeeping while maintaining strong protection of miners. The proposal also includes related conforming amendments.

updates.title: Mozza Foods, Inc.: Availability of a Petition for a Determination of Nonregulated Status and Draft Plant Pest Risk Assessment for MF1786-1 Soybean (Glycine max) Expressing Casein Proteins
updates.abstract: We are advising the public that the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service has received a petition from Mozza Foods, Inc. seeking a determination of nonregulated status for MF1786-1 Soybean (Glycine max) which has been developed using genetic engineering to express the bovine alpha S1, beta and kappa casein proteins and the FAM20C kinase in its seeds, and to reduce the level of soybean glycinin proteins in seeds. We are making the petition and draft plant pest risk assessment available for public review and comment.

updates.title: Unemployment Insurance Program National Minimum Weekly Work Search Requirements
updates.abstract: The U.S. Department of Labor (Department), through the Employment and Training Administration (ETA), is proposing to amend 20 CFR part 604 both to reflect a 2012 update in Federal law in which Congress, by amending section 303(a) of the Social Security Act (SSA), established a Federal work search requirement; and to establish a national minimum weekly work search requirement standard for the Federal-State unemployment compensation (UC) program. This proposed rule would mandate, among other things, that States require individuals claiming UC to complete at least five qualifying work search activities or, where applicable, meet State-adopted points-based system requirements amounting to five qualifying activities or satisfy equivalent labor force attachment criteria, each week for which UC is claimed; that individuals report their work search activities as part of their certification process prior to payment being issued; and that State law allow for certain qualifying work search activities beyond simply employer contacts. This action is necessary to reduce inconsistencies beyond those created by local labor markets in State- level requirements for individuals to actively seek work. The intended effect is to hold States accountable for administering a UC program that provides temporary wage replacement to eligible individuals while they are actively seeking work through a meaningful engagement with the labor market.
